title: Every apply id an Apply writes under is kept on its site_brief row, reused receipts apart, and a finished run's late ids never land on its successor's row
steps: S1: From the TCH checkout run: TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://tracy:tracy@127.0.0.1:51730/postgres node --test --test-reporter=tap apps/tracy-web/test/brief-build.test.mjs apps/tracy-web/test/brief-joomla.test.mjs apps/tracy-web/test/brief-shared.test.mjs apps/tracy-web/test/brief-wordpress.test.mjs (any Postgres whose user may create databases will do — the tests make and drop their own; this one is the local stand's).

S2: Record the exit code, the '# tests', '# pass', '# fail', '# skipped' lines and the result of each case whose name starts with: "every apply id the writes named is kept on the row, in order, once each, a failed run included"; "an apply id this Apply did not mint (the install’s own receipt) is kept apart, so undo reverts only its own"; "a run that is over is stopped, and an id its engine names late never lands on the row of the run that replaced it"; "the door an engine writes through tells the run every apply id a call names, and changes nothing else"; "the door says which apply ids are not this Apply’s own: the fixed demo-trim receipt, and the ones the engine names"; "every apply id the site is written under is told to the run, so the whole Apply can be undone" (2 cases, one in each of brief-joomla.test.mjs and brief-wordpress.test.mjs); "the receipts this Apply reuses — the demo trim’s, the install’s language receipt — are told apart from its own".
expect: S1 exits 0 with '# fail 0' and '# skipped 0', and '# pass' equal to '# tests' (at least 152): the database cases ran, none skipped.

Every named case is 'ok' (none 'not ok', none '# SKIP'): the door an engine writes through reports every apply_id a call names; the row keeps them in timings.applyIds (in order, once each, a failed run included) and the receipts it only reuses (the fixed dtrim-seed, the install’s mlang language receipt) in timings.reusedApplyIds, so undo reverts only its own; an engine of a run that ended never writes ids onto the row of the run that replaced it.
evidence: Ledger L08, 05/10/2026: one Apply writes under several apply ids (dtrim-seed, contract-..., residue-..., tidy-..., mlang-..., facts-..., media-brief-...) and none was stored, so undoing an Apply as one was impossible; review then found reused receipts mixed in and a late run's ids able to land on a new run's row. Reds 83e6c54c9, a9e5d6937, 2bce2049d; fixes 57df42c37, 7f8ae873a, b7e441178.
fence: No door or migration changes; EmDash writes no apply id and keeps none.
